findings.title: Potentially conflicting target labels
findings.finding: 5 feature-identical groups contain more than one non-missing target label.
findings.evidence: 11 labeled rows are included in these groups.
findings.modeling_impact: Inconsistent labels for identical recorded features can introduce irreducible ambiguity or reveal missing time/entity context.
findings.recommendation: Review whether these are label errors, repeated entities over time, target updates, or omitted distinguishing features.
findings.score_effect: Evidence only; this finding does not change any score or guardrail.

findings.title: Duplicate records
findings.finding: Duplicate rows may cause the model to overfit repeated examples or inflate validation confidence.
findings.evidence: 5052 repeated rows (9.38%) across 5040 groups; largest group: 5 rows.
findings.modeling_impact: Repeated examples can be split across training and validation data and make evaluation appear stronger than it is.
findings.recommendation: Deduplicate records or confirm that repeated rows represent legitimate repeated events.
findings.score_effect: Reduces uniqueness and may apply the severe-duplicates guardrail.

findings.title: Target imbalance
findings.finding: The target is dominated by one class, so headline accuracy may hide poor minority-class performance.
findings.evidence: The majority-class baseline is 76.03%; majority-to-minority ratio: 3.17:1.
findings.modeling_impact: A model may favor the majority class and underperform on less common outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Use class-sensitive metrics and consider resampling, weighting, or collecting more minority examples.
findings.score_effect: Reduces the target-balance score and may trigger the critical-sub-score guardrail.

findings.title: Numeric outlier concentration
findings.finding: 1 numeric feature has notable IQR-based outlier rates.
findings.modeling_impact: Extreme values can dominate some model families or indicate collection and unit inconsistencies.
findings.recommendation: Inspect the outlier rows and confirm whether they are real edge cases or data entry errors.
findings.score_effect: Reduces the feature-usability score at the current outlier thresholds.

findings.title: Leakage review prompts
findings.finding: Columns such as marital_status have generic status or target-related names, but their names alone are not strong leakage evidence.
findings.modeling_impact: If a field is only available after the outcome, offline validation may not represent deployment.
findings.recommendation: Confirm when these values become available; this review prompt does not reduce the leakage score or cap the overall score.
findings.score_effect: Evidence only; review-only leakage prompts do not change a score or guardrail.

conflicting_target_labels.title: Potentially conflicting target labels
observed: 5 feature-identical groups (11 rows) with more than one non-missing label.
impact: Identical recorded inputs with different outcomes limit how well any model can fit those cases.
Conflicts may reflect omitted context, outcomes that are genuinely random, or annotation differences.
investigate: A sample of conflicting groups: what distinguishes them that the file does not record.
Whether conflicts concentrate in one source, annotator or period.

options.option: Keep all rows and treat the variation as real
options.prerequisites: The variation is plausible for the outcome.
options.avoid_when: One label is known to be wrong.
options.verify: Report the conflicting share alongside model results.

options.prerequisites: A reviewer or reference can decide the correct label.
options.avoid_when: No reliable reference exists; majority voting would invent certainty.
options.verify: Record changed labels and re-run this analysis.

options.option: Add the missing context as features
options.prerequisites: The distinguishing information exists and is available at prediction time.
options.avoid_when: The added information is only known after the outcome.
options.verify: Re-check repeated-input conflicts with the added features.

duplicate_records.title: Duplicate records
observed: 5,052 of 53,842 rows repeat an earlier row (9.38%), in 5,040 groups; largest group 5 rows.
impact: Identical rows give repeated cases more weight.
If copies land on both sides of a train/test split, evaluation can look better than it will be on new data.
investigate: Whether repetition reflects genuine repeated events (the same values recurring legitimately) or copying.
Whether an identifier or timestamp exists that would make repeated rows distinct.

options.option: Keep repeated rows but split by group
options.prerequisites: An identifier or the full row can define groups.
options.verify: Confirm that no group appears in more than one split.

options.prerequisites: Repetition is confirmed to be copying, not repeated events.
options.avoid_when: Rows are legitimate repeated observations; removing them changes the represented frequencies.
options.verify: Report row counts and class shares before and after; re-run this analysis on the result.

unknowns: Whether repeated rows are legitimate repeated events or copies was not assessed.

target_imbalance.title: Target imbalance
impact: Accuracy can look high while the minority class is mostly missed.
Default decision thresholds and probability outputs may suit the majority class.
investigate: Whether the observed class shares match the population the model will serve.
How many minority rows each later split will contain.

options.avoid_when: Not applicable: this changes no data.
options.verify: Report per-class precision and recall, precision–recall curves and the confusion matrix at the chosen threshold, on a held-out split.

options.option: Choose class weights or a decision threshold
options.prerequisites: The relative cost of each error type is known or can be stated.
options.avoid_when: Calibrated probabilities are the deliverable and will not be recalibrated afterwards.
options.verify: Compare per-class metrics and calibration before and after, on the same split.

options.prerequisites: Rows are independent, and resampling happens inside training folds only.
options.avoid_when: Rows are grouped or time-ordered so resampled copies would cross splits; or resampling would precede the train/test split.
options.verify: Check minority-class metrics on untouched validation data; confirm no resampled row appears in evaluation.

options.prerequisites: More examples can be obtained from the same population.
options.avoid_when: New examples come from a different population.
options.verify: Re-run this analysis and compare class shares and feature distributions by source.

numeric_outlier_concentration.title: Numeric outlier concentration
observed: hours_per_week: 14,849 of 53,842 rows (27.58%) outside the 1.5 × IQR fences; q1 40, q3 45, min 1, max 99; 0 negative, 0 zero.
Under this policy the denominator is all rows, and non-finite values count as outside the fences.
IQR is zero for capital_gain, capital_loss (q1 equals q3), so the fences cannot separate values; the recorded rate of 0 there means 'not assessable', not 'no outliers'.
impact: Values outside the 1.5 × IQR fences can dominate scale-sensitive methods and summary statistics.
They may be legitimate tails, unit or entry errors, or sentinel codes.
investigate: The extreme values themselves: are they plausible for the field's meaning and unit?
Whether a single code (for example −1 or 999) accounts for many of them.

options.option: Keep the values and use robust methods or transforms
options.avoid_when: They are confirmed errors or sentinel codes.
options.verify: Compare model behaviour with and without the transform on the same split.

options.prerequisites: Extremes are legitimate but over-influential, and the cap is chosen from training rows only.
options.avoid_when: Tails carry the signal you care about (for example, fraud amounts); or the cap uses evaluation data.
options.verify: Report how many values change and compare metrics on tail cases specifically.

options.prerequisites: They are confirmed errors from source records.
options.verify: Re-run this analysis and record which rows changed.

unknowns: Whether extreme values are legitimate was not assessed; an IQR flag does not establish an error.
